title: SCENES Dataset
text: The SCENES Dataset is an international collaborative effort to characterize and analyze naturalistic visual environments across different geographies. The project brings together partners from around the globe to build a rich repository of spectral and spatial data.

import re
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from itertools import product

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")


Load dataset

fpath = "../data/20250630_SCENES_metadata_integrated_modified.xlsx"
meta_integrated = pd.read_excel(fpath)

meta_df = meta_integrated.copy()


def extract_parentheses_content(scene):
    scene = str(scene).strip()
    match = re.search(r'\((.*?)\)', scene)
    if match:
        return match.group(1).strip()
    else:
        return ""
    
if "scene" in meta_df:
    meta_df["scene"] = meta_df["scene"].apply(extract_parentheses_content)
if "lighting" in meta_df:
    meta_df["lighting"] = meta_df["lighting"].apply(extract_parentheses_content)


meta_df.columns

Index(['record', 'project_id', 'project_name', 'project_start', 'data_curator',
       'project_record', 'setup', 'device_geometry', 'measurement_id',
       'record_id', 'date', 'time', 'protocol', 'experimenter',
       'available_$device', 'available_gloptic_spectis1',
       'available_gigahertz-optic_msc15', 'available_jeti_spectraval1511',
       'available_westborophotonics_wp690e-circ', 'wp690csv',
       'available_kleininstruments_k-10a', 'available_inteldrealsense_d455',
       'available_gopro_hero10black_video',
       'available_gopro_hero10black_photo', 'location', 'latitude',
       'longitude', 'direction', 'elevation', 'groundheight', 'boxtilt',
       'boxheight', 'temperature', 'humidity', 'weather', 'other_weather',
       'wind', 'scene', 'other_scene', 'view', 'other_view', 'lighting',
       'other_lighting', 'technotes', 'available_all', 'hour'],
      dtype='object')



VIEW_COLORS = {
    "Outdoor": "#CD923B",
    "Indoor w/ window": "#081A5B",
    "Indoor w/o window":  "#426E56"
}


meta_df['hour'] = meta_df['time'].astype(str).str.zfill(4).str[:2].astype(int)
meta_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(meta_df['date'], format="%Y%m%d")
meta_df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(meta_df["date"], errors="coerce").dt.date
meta_df = meta_df.sort_values("date")


counts = (
    meta_df.dropna(subset=["date","view"])
           .groupby(["date","view"]).size()
           .unstack("view", fill_value=0)
)

full_idx = pd.date_range(counts.index.min(), counts.index.max(), freq="D").date
counts = counts.reindex(full_idx, fill_value=0)
counts.index.name = "date"

long_df = counts.reset_index().melt(id_vars="date", var_name="view", value_name="count")
long_df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(long_df["date"])

fig = px.bar(
    long_df,
    x="date", y="count", color="view",
    color_discrete_map=VIEW_COLORS,
    title="Indoor vs Outdoor by date"
)

fig.update_layout(
    bargap=0.01,
    barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title=None,
    yaxis_title="Count",
    legend_title="",
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",       
        yanchor="bottom",      
        y=1.02,                
        xanchor="center",      
        x=0.5,
    ),
    height=500,
)

fig.update_xaxes(tickangle=305)
fig.show()

fig.write_html("../assets/plots/daily_stacked_by_view.html", include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=False)

Unable to display output for mime type(s): application/vnd.plotly.v1+json




meta_df = meta_df.copy()
meta_df["hour"] = pd.to_numeric(meta_df["hour"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
meta_df = meta_df.dropna(subset=["hour", "view"])
meta_df["hour"] = meta_df["hour"].astype(int).clip(0, 23)

hour_counts = (
    meta_df.groupby(["hour", "view"])
           .size()
           .reset_index(name="count")
)

hours = pd.Index(range(24), name="hour")
views = pd.Index([v for v in VIEW_COLORS if v in meta_df["view"].unique()], name="view")
full = (
    pd.MultiIndex.from_product([hours, views], names=["hour", "view"])
    .to_frame(index=False)
)
hour_counts = (
    full.merge(hour_counts, on=["hour", "view"], how="left")
        .fillna({"count": 0})
)
hour_counts["count"] = hour_counts["count"].astype(int)

fig = px.bar(
    hour_counts,
    x="hour", y="count",
    color="view",
    barmode="group",
    color_discrete_map=VIEW_COLORS,
    title="Acquisitions by hour of day"
)

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(dtick=1, title="Hour of Day"),
    yaxis_title="Count",
    bargap=0.1,
    bargroupgap=0.05,
    legend_title="",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="center", x=0.5),

fig.show()

# --- inputs / orders ---
custom_scene_order = [
    'countryside', 'forest', 'water', 'skyscraper', 'mountain',
    'park', 'city', 'open field', 'industry', 'road',
    'office', 'conference room', 'corridor', 'bedroom', 'kitchen'
]
view_order = ["Outdoor", "Indoor w/ window", "Indoor w/o window"]

# --- aggregate counts like your matplotlib code ---
combo_counts = (
    meta_df.groupby(['scene', 'view', 'lighting'])
           .size().reset_index(name='count')
           .sort_values('count', ascending=False)
)
agg_counts = combo_counts.groupby(['scene', 'view'], as_index=False)['count'].sum()

# keep only scenes present in data but respect your custom order
scenes_in_data = [s for s in custom_scene_order if s in agg_counts['scene'].unique()]

# build full grid scene×view so missing combos show as 0 (keeps stacking consistent)
full = pd.DataFrame(list(product(scenes_in_data, view_order)), columns=['scene','view'])
plot_df = (full.merge(agg_counts, on=['scene','view'], how='left')
                .fillna({'count': 0}))
plot_df['count'] = plot_df['count'].astype(int)

# --- plotly stacked bar with inside labels ---
fig = px.bar(
    plot_df,
    x='scene', y='count', color='view',
    category_orders={'scene': scenes_in_data, 'view': view_order},
    color_discrete_map=VIEW_COLORS,
    title="Scene distribution by view",
    # text_auto=True,

fig.update_layout(
    barmode='stack',
    xaxis_title=None,

    legend_title='',
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='center', x=0.5),

    bargap=0.15

scene_order = sorted(meta_df["scene"].dropna().unique())

fig = px.box(
    meta_df.dropna(subset=["scene", "hour", "view"]),

title: SCENES Overview
text: This page gives a quick look at what’s inside the dataset. It shows how the images are distributed by view type, time, scene, weather, and lighting. Each section highlights the main patterns you can spot from the plots.

title: SCENES Overview
text:
View
Outdoor shots make up the largest part of the dataset. Indoor scenes are split between spaces with windows (plenty of natural light) and enclosed rooms without windows. This balance makes it possible to compare natural vs. artificial lighting conditions.

title: SCENES Overview
text:
Temporal
Data collection happened in bursts over several months, reflecting field campaigns and site availability. Outdoor shots are more evenly spread, while indoor sessions are clustered into shorter time windows.
                        
                                            

Most captures were taken between 9 AM and 5 PM, peaking around midday. That matches typical daylight hours but still leaves good coverage in the morning and late afternoon.

title: SCENES Overview
text:
Scene
The dataset covers a mix of environments. On the outdoor side, countryside and forest dominate, while for indoor shots, offices lead the way, with some extra coverage from conference rooms, corridors, and bedrooms.
                        
                                            

Capture times follow expectations: outdoor scenes center on the middle of the day, while indoor environments stretch later into the afternoon.

title: SCENES Overview
text:
Weather & Lighting
Most images come from clear or partly cloudy days. There’s also a fair amount of overcast/cloudy coverage, which helps include softer light. Rare conditions like rain, fog, drizzle, and snow are present but limited.
                        
                                            

Lighting conditions are mostly daylight, with a smaller but useful set of mixed light (daylight + electric) and a handful of purely artificial light samples. This gives the dataset range across natural and human-made lighting setups.
                        
                                            



Overall, the dataset offers a broad mix of outdoor and indoor scenes, captured across different times of day, seasons, weather conditions, and lighting setups. Outdoor shots dominate, but there’s still solid coverage of indoor environments, including both naturally lit and windowless spaces.
This diversity is intentional: it makes the dataset useful for studying how context (scene, weather, or lighting) affects image appearance and for training models that need to generalize beyond a single environment. In other words, the numbers and plots above aren’t just statistics — they set the stage for building models that are robust to real-world variability.
